title.narrative: Kenya 2017 Drought Emergency Response in Marsabit and West Pokot Counties

description.narrative:
Kenya is facing a severe drought, which is because of failed rains in MAM and OCD long and short rains, respectively. On 10 February 2017, the Government declared a national drought emergency, with 23 of 47 counties affected. The number of food insecure people more than doubled – from 1.3 million to 2.7 million and then 3.0 million people in March. Marsabit( Marsabit diocese) and West Pokot(Kitale diocese) counties are among the worst affected
Water access and availability has been adversely affected in these areas, with populations having to go through longer walking distances to the scarce water points, since the water points are also drying up, as well as very long waiting times. In Marsabit, for example, the major sources of water for livestock currently is boreholes, which was not normal at this time of the year as the main source is usually water pans. In some places, such as Moyale, Kalacha, Dukana and Gatab shallow wells, water pans and springs were being used. The return trekking distances from grazing areas to water points is 50-70 kilometres for camels, 20-30 kilometres for cattle and 15-25 kilometres for small stock in agro pastoral and pastoral livelihood zones (KFSSG , 2017).
Humanitarian interventions by the Government of Kenya, at both the national and county-level, as well as by other development partners, across various parts of the pastoral and marginal agricultural areas, are likely mitigating the severity of acute food insecurity outcomes. However, insufficient and uncoordinated response efforts to date, in some areas, and lack of clarity on numbers of planned beneficiaries and coverage areas, make it difficult to assess the impacts of the humanitarian assistance and future. FEWSNET has projected that without adequate and sustained humanitarian assistance, more poor households could face Emergency (IPC Phase 4) outcomes between the dry period of July and September, particularly in Marsabit. In response to the appeal by Caritas international, CAFOD will contribute £50,000 to Caritas Kenya as part of the intervention in Marsabit and West Pokot Counties.
